title: Runtime: load hardware tuning profile based on GPU SKU (override order + safe fallback)
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: - Runtime can now auto-select a hardware tuning profile by detected GPU SKU with explicit override precedence and safe fallbacks. - Adds startup logging for detection + selection source to reduce misconfig risk in Dedicated/Private.
description: Context: This PR wires up runtime-side hardware detection + profile selection for the hardware tuning profiles pack. The schema + validation landed in pr-21984; this change is the runtime integration layer that (a) detects GPU SKU at startup, (b) selects the best matching profile from the pack, (c) applies an explicit override order, and (d) fails safe when detection is ambiguous or unsupported. Motivation: We need predictable, supportable defaults across Hosted/Dedicated/Private without requiring per-pool manual configuration, while still allowing controlled overrides for canaries and customer environments. Summary of behavior (override order): 1) Explicit per-process override: REDWOOD_RUNTIME_HW_PROFILE (exact profile id). 2) Per-deployment override file: runtime_config.hardware_profile_id (e.g., set via Helm/values or local config). 3) Fleet/pool default: runtime_config.hardware_profile_family (e.g., "h100", "l40s") when ops wants a coarse pin without relying on SKU parsing. 4) Auto-detect: detect GPU SKU and map to family + variant using normalized device strings. 5) Safe fallback: if detection is unknown/ambiguous, select "generic" profile (conservative knobs) and emit a structured warning; runtime continues serving. Hardware detection details: - Uses NVML when available to fetch device name + PCI IDs; falls back to nvidia-smi parsing in minimal environments. - Normalizes common provider string variants (e.g., "NVIDIA H100 PCIe", "NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3", "NVIDIA H100 SXM") into canonical sku_family values (h100/b200/l40s) and sku_form_factor when available. - Handles MIG by treating the node as a family match but refusing to pick aggressive profiles that assume full device memory; we default to "family" profile unless an explicit profile id override is provided. - Multi-GPU nodes: selects one profile for the runtime process; if mixed families are detected (should not happen in prod pools), we warn and fall back to "generic" unless explicitly overridden. Guardrails / safety: - Any profile selected via auto-detect must pass schema validation + compatibility check (runtime min/max version) or we fall back to "generic". - We never hard-fail startup on detection errors; we fail open with conservative defaults and actionable logs. - Adds a metric label for selection_source (override_env, override_config, fleet_default, auto_detect, fallback) to enable rollout analysis (full dashboard work continues in pr-22027 / observability-pack). Logging: - On startup, logs a single-line summary: detected GPU info, normalized sku_family, selected profile id, selection_source, and fallback_reason when applicable. - In debug logs, prints the candidate matching path (exact match -> family match -> generic). Tests: - Unit tests for normalization against a table of real-world device strings from infra threads (PCIe vs SXM variants, cloud provider prefixes). - Integration test for override precedence (env > config > fleet default > auto-detect) with a fake NVML provider. - Regression test: unknown GPU string should not crash and should select generic with warning. Rollout plan: - Gate is runtime-only; actual tuned profiles remain controlled by pack versioning and per-pool enablement. - We will canary in a single H100 pool first; SRE asked that we ensure fallback remains silent-noisy (warn once) rather than spamming logs per request. Related: - pr-21984-add-hardware-profile-schema-and-json-validation (schema + validator) - ENG-4823 (loader + precedence) - SUP-29438 (Private customer request re: overriding profiles safely; this PR supports deterministic precedence and debuggability).
changed_areas: Changed areas/files (high level): - runtime/config/hardware_profiles/selector.ts: new selection module (override order + matching). - runtime/config/hardware_profiles/normalize_gpu.ts: GPU string normalization + MIG detection heuristics. - runtime/platform/nvml.ts: thin wrapper around NVML with safe fallbacks. - runtime/startup/logging.ts: startup log line for profile selection summary. - runtime/metrics/runtime_info.ts: adds selection_source label and selected_profile_id gauge (low-cardinality). - runtime/tests/hardware_profile_selector.test.ts: precedence + fallback tests. - runtime/tests/gpu_normalization_golden.test.ts: table-driven normalization coverage. Snippet (illustrative): selector precedence: if (envProfileId) return selectById(envProfileId, 'override_env'); if (config.profileId) return selectById(config.profileId, 'override_config'); if (config.profileFamily) return selectByFamily(config.profileFamily, 'fleet_default'); const detected = detectGpuFamily(); if (!detected) return selectGeneric('fallback', 'gpu_detection_failed'); return selectByDetectedSku(detected, 'auto_detect');
commits: runtime: add gpu sku normalization + detection adapter
runtime: implement hardware profile selector with precedence + fallback
runtime: add startup logs + runtime_info metrics for selection source
tests: golden coverage for gpu name variants + MIG behavior
docs: inline comments on override order + operational intent
review_conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can you spell out precedence in-code and ensure we never throw on unknown GPUs? Also please avoid selecting an H100 variant profile on MIG by default; we’ve seen memory assumptions bite us. Benji Okafor (author): Added explicit precedence constants + comments in selector.ts and changed MIG path to family-only unless explicit profile id override is set. Unknown/ambiguous now always selects generic and logs a single warning. Irene Choi (review): The GPU name variants list is incomplete; we have at least 3 strings for H100 across providers. Please include the ones from the infra thread and add a unit test so we don’t regress. Benji Okafor (author): Added golden table cases for the provider variants we’ve observed and wired normalization to strip provider prefixes consistently. Sofia Ivanova (review): For mixed-family multi-GPU nodes: do we ever want to pick the “first device” and proceed? I’d rather fail safe. Benji Okafor (author): Agreed; mixed-family now triggers fallback to generic unless overridden. Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Logging looks good but please ensure the warning is once-per-startup, not per-request, and keep labels low cardinality. Benji Okafor (author): Confirmed: warning emitted at startup only; metrics are selected_profile_id (bounded by pack) + selection_source enum. Noah Patel (review): Please add a compatibility check hook so a new pack version can declare min runtime version. Benji Okafor (author): Added validator gate: incompatible profiles are rejected and we fall back to generic with reason 'incompatible_profile'. Approvals: Ethan Park approved; Irene Choi approved; Sean Gallagher approved after latest push.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4828 (perf canary gates) and pr-22027 (expanded metrics + debug endpoint).
